analysis.title: The OpenAI "Tell": BofA Says The AI Bubble Will Burst With Stocks AND Yields Tumbling... Here Is The Cheapest Hedge
key_insights: BofA's equity-linked team calls the Oct 8 OpenAI revenue report the 'tell'. The FT reported OpenAI's annualized revenue near $50B at end of September, about $20B below figures floated weeks earlier. The Nasdaq fell 1.4%, with semis (SOX) down 3.4% and memory (DRAM) down 5.1%. BofA calls it one of the cleanest case studies of how equities might react to a prolonged AI slowdown.

The Nasdaq's underperformance versus the S&P on Oct 8 matched the gap on every other AI-specific risk-off day since DeepSeek in January 2025. BofA attributes this to the Nasdaq's beta to the private-side AI ecosystem and keeps the Nasdaq as its index of choice for any AI trade, long or short.

Yields fell together with equities on Oct 8 and held the move through the close. DeepSeek in January 2025 showed the same pattern. This contrasts with the 'equities lower, yields higher' regime of recent months, in which bonds have not hedged equities. The 2000 dotcom unwind is a third precedent: 10Y yields fell from roughly 6.5% to the mid-4s as the Nasdaq 100 dropped.
BofA argues an AI slowdown would hit growth and inflation (less capex, less power and resource consumption), pushing yields lower on top of the usual flight-to-safety bid.

On Oct 14, core CPI came in hot and October rate-hike odds briefly spiked above 50%. 10Y yields reversed the initial CPI spike and finished roughly unchanged as AI credit fears took over, with the article citing the view that the end of the AI boom would be 'massively deflationary'.

CoreWeave (CRWV) fell more than 15% on Oct 14, its third-biggest drop on record. Its 2032 bonds had blown through 1,000bps of G-spread and a 15% yield the day before. CDS closed 135bps wider and the credit market prices a 63% chance of default within five years. D.A. Davidson's Gil Luria calls it the 'subprime tranche' of AI, says the equity goes to zero if it can't service its debt, and notes it borrows at about 9% while earning about 1% on investments.

Contagion on Oct 14: Gartner said 80% of neoclouds will cease independent operations by 2030. DigitalOcean fell 14%, Hut 8 10%, Nebius and IREN 9%, Oracle 9%. The NDX and Russell both fell about 2%. AI stocks lag the S&P ex-AI by 840bps this week.
BTIG's Jonathan Krinsky argues the pain trade is 'rates down, Nasdaq down', and that Mag7 falling with rates would add conviction to his 'Red October' call.

Hedge 1 (NDX): buy Sep27 90% max lookback put (daily observations), contingent on 10y SOFR below ATMf minus 25bps, for 3.62% indicatively. That is a 46% discount to the max lookback put and 23bps cheaper than a vanilla put (ref. 30904, 4.919%). The max lookback strike resets higher as the market rallies, and the rates contingency more than funds that feature. Risk is the upfront premium.

Backtest of a Sep-27-equivalent structure over 30 years at today's levels: 13% hit rate versus 11% for a vanilla 90% put. Average in-the-money payout was 7.2x versus 6.1x for the vanilla put and 3.9x for the plain lookback. The largest outperformance came in the dotcom bust.

Primary risk to the NDX hybrid is a 2022-style 'equity down, rates up' crash, where an inflation or Fed shock swamps the AI unwind. The article notes this is not a tail risk given how bonds traded in 2026 and the hot CPI. For aggressive users, selling an 80% put against it for another 50%+ discount gives something like an expanding put spread. Selling a same-strike vanilla put makes the package a net credit.

BofA's Bubble Risk Indicator: only 13 S&P 500 stocks have a BRI above 0.8, 2.4% of index weight, versus 50-100 stocks and 20-40% of market cap at the dotcom peak. Highest single names: Moderna, CrowdStrike, HPE, Zebra, Revvity, Palo Alto. BofA's US Cyber Security and Brazil Election baskets each screen at 0.92. The froth is concentrated in pockets. The article adds Jefferies' view (Oct 10) that this is AI's 2008 moment, with two cash-burning labs owing half of a $2.3 trillion backlog.

S&P 5-day intraday realized vol is 7.6%, the 3rd percentile of the past year. BofA says elevated SPX hedger gamma has acted as a guardrail on intraday moves. The latest reading was $14.5bn as of Oct 9 (4th highest in a year), after readings ranking 2nd and 3rd highest over the prior two weeks. Part of the build reflects increased 1DTE selling flow.

Gamma levels per Bloomberg and SpotGamma: the S&P broke its first pressure points at 7,775-7,750 on Oct 14, SpotGamma's volatility trigger is 7,775, and below about 7,700 positive gamma thins sharply. Michael Ball warns weakness increasingly produces more weakness.

Customers are piling into VIX calls, with positioning approaching summer 2024 levels. The SPX term structure is steep, with the 1-month vs 1-week ATMf implied vol ratio in the 95th percentile of the past year. With positions unchanged, a 10-point shock to front-month VIX futures would force dealers to buy about 90% of daily VIX futures volume to stay delta neutral, the highest in a year. Investor monetization of VIX calls may dampen a spike while dealer re-hedging may amplify it.

Hedge 2 (VIX): buy VIX Nov 19-24 call spread for $0.63 indicatively on mids, with a 7.9x max payout ratio (about 45d/25d strikes, UXX6 ref. 17.61). Risk is the upfront premium. BofA expects the midterms to be a dispersion event more than a vol event, so the spread targets a modest VIX rise. VIX was back above 17 on Oct 14.

Goldman's desk argued on Oct 12 there is a higher probability of VIX 25 than SPX -2%, as hedge funds sell tech while conviction is at record lows. Derivatives and income fund AUM is $322B, up $222B since 2020, with combined fund and exotic vega supply of 415 million vega per month.

S&P 3M implied vol was 13.7 in BofA's latest tally, before the Oct 14 VIX rise. Upcoming catalysts are PPI (Oct 15), Anthropic's numbers and big-tech earnings later in October. The author says that if the S&P can't reclaim 7,750, dealers won't catch it.

risk_factors: A 2022-style 'equity down, rates up' selloff would defeat the rates-contingent NDX hedge, and the hot Oct 14 CPI and higher rate-hike odds make it plausible.
Dealer gamma could stop cushioning the S&P if it stays below the 7,775-7,750 area, and positive gamma thins sharply under about 7,700.
A liquidity air pocket akin to August 2024 could amplify a VIX spike through dealer re-hedging.
Neocloud credit stress, including CoreWeave's debt service and capital markets access, could spread to AI equities and Oracle.
Private-side AI stress such as OpenAI's revenue gap and Anthropic's numbers could transmit to public markets.

tension_points.bull_case: The AI bubble has years left to run, with bubble froth confined to pockets (13 S&P stocks, 2.4% of weight, versus 20-40% at the dotcom peak) and dip buyers absorbing the Oct 8 OpenAI scare within a session.
tension_points.bear_case: AI disappointments hit the Nasdaq first and hardest while yields fall. The OpenAI revenue gap and CoreWeave's credit stress show cracks, and the bond market would again act as a hedge in a prolonged AI slowdown.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 2022-style equity-down, rates-up crash would invalidate the rates-contingent hedge. Separately, the S&P failing to reclaim 7,750 removes the dealer gamma cushion.

tension_points.bull_case: Realized vol is at the 3rd percentile, dip buying is steady, correlation is low, tech is resilient, and elevated dealer hedger gamma guards intraday moves.
tension_points.bear_case: The calm is held up by 0DTE/1DTE selling and income fund supply. With steep term structure and heavy VIX call positioning, dealer re-hedging could amplify a spike beyond what the stock move implies.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The S&P holding above SpotGamma's 7,775 volatility trigger keeps dealer hedging dampening moves. Trading below about 7,700 thins positive gamma sharply.
